title: GPU hot-swap and cluster scale playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for on-call SREs handling GPU node failures, live GPU replacement (hot-swap), node cordon/drain nuances for model-serving workloads, cluster recovery after multi-node incidents, and planned capacity add steps.

Status & scope:
- WIP: contains operational run-steps, safety checks, and TODOs.
- Focused on Redwood Dedicated + Private clusters (k8s on-prem / cloud-gpu pools).
- Assumes familiarity with redwoodctl, kubectl, PagerDuty, and our incident ticketing flow.

Pre-incident checklist (fast preflight when pager goes off):
1) Identify alert: note alert source (monitoring, PodOOM, GPU ECC error, BMC).
2) PagerDuty: acknowledge and open INC ticket (prefix INFRA-).
3) Look up affected nodes:
   - rwdctl nodes list --filter "gpu_error"  OR use Datadog host tags
   - kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep <node-name>
4) Check model-serving criticality: which routes/models use the node? ping product oncall if customer-facing SLA risk.

Quick triage commands (common):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl cordon <node>
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=120
- rwdctl node describe <node>  # internal agent status, GPU health flags
- ssh admin@<node> sudo nvidia-smi -q  # check ECC, thermal, driver state
- ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin -P **** power status  # if BMC accessible

If node has transient GPU process hang (soft failure):
- Try restarting GPU drivers before drain if latency-sensitive and pods are tolerant:
  - sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker  OR  sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia
  - Check pod health. If restart resolves, document steps and tag INC ticket with mitigation.
- If restart fails or GPU shows hardware faults (ECC/retired pages), proceed to cordon/drain and plan replacement.

Cordon & drain guidance (preserve model state where possible):
- Prefer graceful drain for nodes in the Hosted model-serving tier: 2-5 minute grace if pods have checkpointing.
- Use low-impact draining windows for Dedicated pools serving non-production traffic where possible.
- Commands:
  1) kubectl cordon <node>  # prevents new pods scheduling
  2) kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
  3) kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
- If pods stuck in Terminating due to stuck volume detach or grpc connections, escalate to storage or networking owners and consider force deletion as last resort:
  - kubectl delete pod <pod> --force --grace-period=0
  - Note: forced deletes risk lost in-flight requests for model-serving (document in incident ticket).

GPU hot-swap / replacement (physical swap on-prem or cloud instance type swap):
- Preconditions: node drained, cordoned, and workloads verified migrated.
- If on-prem (rack GPU replacement):
  1) Tag node in inventory and update INC ticket with serial and chassis location.
  2) Put BMC into maintenance mode and power down via ipmitool.
  3) Replace GPU module following vendor ESD and torque specs.
  4) Power on, verify POST. ssh in, check dmesg and nvidia-smi.
  5) Run driver/firmware quick-check: install vendor recommended firmware if mismatch.
  6) Run rwdctl node health-check and mark ready.
- If in cloud (preemptible/GPU attach issues):
  1) Either reprovision a fresh node with the same labels and let autoscaler rebalance OR attach new GPU to VM if supported.
  2) Validate CUDA / driver compatibility (we standardize on CUDA 11.x or 12.x depending on pool).
  3) Rejoin node to cluster.

Reintegration & post-swap checks:
- kubectl uncordon <node>  # only after node passes health checks
- rwdctl node validate <node>  # internal validation run (agent + gpu tests)
- Run smoke test traffic against model-serving on the node: run synthetic requests to verify throughput and latency.
- Monitor for regression: increased 5xx, token latency, or error rates for 30 minutes.

Cluster recovery after multi-node or control-plane impact:
- If etcd or control plane degraded: follow control-plane recovery runbook (link TODO).
- If many worker nodes impacted (OOM storms / GPU firmware bug):
  1) Stop autoscaler to prevent churn while we stabilize: rwdctl autoscaler pause
  2) Quarantine affected node image/version: mark image as bad in inventory.
  3) Scale up temporary capacity from staging or spare-pool: rwdctl pool add --name temp-gpu-pool --count 3 --type a100-40
  4) Drain and reprovision affected nodes in batches (3 at a time max) to avoid schedule storms.
  5) Resume autoscaler only after validation.

Planned capacity add (predictable scale ops):
- Pre-ops: update capacity plan doc, notify stakeholders, schedule low-traffic window if possible.
- Steps:
  1) rwdctl pool create --size <n> --gpu-type <type> --labels "dedicated=true,zone=us-west"
  2) Wait for nodes to join and pass health checks (rwdctl pool status).
  3) Warm caches: run sample inference to populate KV cache and model artifact caches on new nodes.
  4) Monitor per-token cost and latency metrics for 2 hours; rollback if anomalies.

Escalation matrix (who to contact):
- SRE oncall (pager) -> primary: Ethan Ramirez -> secondary: Priya Shah -> manager: Noah Li
- Hardware vendor escalation: contact ops-hw@redwood with serial and logs (include dmesg, nvidia-smi).
- Product oncall if customer-facing latency SLA risk.

Common troubleshooting notes & gotchas:
- Do NOT uncordon node if kernel oopses appear in dmesg; those cause random pod failures. Reimage instead.
- Avoid force-deleting pods that are writing model state without notifying product teams.
- Some older kernels require nvidia-driver rollback after firmware update — keep driver rollback artifacts in /opt/gpu-drivers/rollback.
- MIG-enabled GPUs: ensure proper MIG slice restore script runs on node join (rwdctl mig restore).

Post-incident / incident review actions (to include in ticket):
- Summary: what failed, impact window, affected customers/routes.
- Root cause hypothesis: hardware, driver, firmware, or software-level regression.
- Mitigation applied and time to mitigation.
- Recovery steps and time to full recovery.
- Followups: firmware upgrades, driver pins, capacity buffers, test coverage for hot-swap.
- Owners for followups and target dates.

TODOs / open items:
- Add links to control-plane recovery runbook (missing).
- Capture standard driver versions per GPU pool in a central table.
- Add automated smoke test job that runs on node join (rwdctl hook).

Appendix: useful commands quick reference
- kubectl cordon <node>
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- kubectl uncordon <node>
- rwdctl node describe <node>
- rwdctl node validate <node>
- ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U <user> -P <pass> chassis power status

Notes to self (fragile / in-progress):
- Consider adding a safety gate in Console to prevent uncordon if last 5-minute error rate > X.
- Investigate automating GPU firmware checks in CI for node images.

End of doc (WIP)
